introduction: My name is David, and I have always been passionate about programming. I completed my Computer Engineering degree at the University of Las Palmas de Gran Canaria in 2022, and in 2025 I went on to finish my Master’s degree at the University of Limerick.

Over the years, I have gained knowledge and experience in developing software products using programming languages such as Java, C++, C#, JavaScript and Python. The projects I have worked on adhere to Clean Code principles, utilise architectural models like MVC, as well as design patterns such as Command and Observer.

projects.name: Argivo - Declarative Command-Line Framework for Bash
projects.skills: Bash, GNU/Linux, CLI, Argument Parsing, Shell Scripting
projects.description: Argivo is a declarative command-line framework that turns Bash functions into documented commands through a simple annotation-based syntax. It provides function-based commands, declarative metadata, a built-in standard library and automatic help generation without requiring additional argument-parsing code.

featured.title: Argivo
featured.summary: Declarative framework that turns Bash functions into documented commands.

projects.name: Canarias Flavor Pack
projects.description: Canarias Flavor Pack is a mod for CK3 focused on the historical and cultural representation of the indigenous peoples and their traditions in the Canary Islands. An effort has been made to represent the islands as faithfully as possible, based on historical sources or plausible assumptions.

projects.name: Migrating and Refactoring a Network Visualisation Application
projects.skills: React, TypeScript, Three.js, WebGL, Graph Algorithms, Network Visualisation, Software Refactoring
projects.description: The main objective of this project is to enhance the quality of NetvizGL through two complementary approaches. On the one hand, the project aims to migrate the application from a desktop-based architecture to a web-based platform. On the other hand, it intends to apply systematic refactoring techniques to the new codebase to improve its overall maintainability, extensibility, and usability.

featured.title: Netviz Web
featured.summary: Web migration and refactoring of a network visualisation application using React, TypeScript and Three.js.

projects.name: Expedia - Expedient Manager
projects.skills: Teamwork, Git, Test-Driven Development (TDD), Gherkin, Behavior-Driven Development (BDD), Communication, Maven, Bash, Java
projects.description: Expedia is a desktop application designed for the efficient management of general entry records and expedients processed by the Industry and Commerce Service of the Cabildo de Gran Canaria. The main objective of this project is to facilitate Service workers to monitor the status and evolution of each of the processed records, optimizing certain repetitive tasks and reducing possible human errors.

projects.name: Design and Implementation of a Generic Lexical Analysis Engine of source code for VPL
projects.skills: PHP, Moodle, GNU/Linux, Behat, PHPUnit, Docker, Git, Visual Studio Code, Sphinx
projects.description: Lexical analysis engine for VPL that improves the lexical processing with the lexical definition of the programming languages from external JSON files called rules files. This final degree project greatly facilitates the incorporation of programming languages for the lexical analysis performed in the early phases of the VPL similarity search. Besides, it is an adaptation of the current Ace source code editor tokenizer.

featured.title: VPL Lexical Analysis Engine
featured.summary: Configurable lexical analysis engine based on JSON rules, developed as a final degree project.
